matches.quote: On p. 10, "delayed rise and slower decay of the intensity in the X valleys (blue curve)" should say red curve
The momentum microscope also records the valence band (Fig. 1a), so pump-induced depletion at the VBM (Y)... would directly test the predicted electron–hole mirror behaviour
under ZZ pumping the holes depolarize and reverse on the same timescale, so the electron–hole pair, and any optical readout of it, is not nonvolatile in either channel
Figs. 2(e,f) plot "Norm. Int."... The authors should calibrate the relative X/Y photoemission efficiency in each geometry... from calculated cross-sections
The early AC map (Fig. 2b) has a high, structured background... show the unnormalized per-valley X and Y intensities for both pump geometries on a common scale
neither the absorbed fluence nor the carrier density is given and only one fluence is shown... The authors should give the absorbed densities for both configurations
Unidirectional relaxation toward the lower valley is generic to nondegenerate multivalley semiconductors... which have been studied extensively with ultrafast optics and photoemission.
An experimental test, such as the temperature dependence of the AC decay time (n_q vs n_q + 1, e.g. 80 K vs 300 K)... would substantially strengthen it.

notes: For C1, the review does not use the phrase 'signal-to-noise ratio' but notes the high background in the AC map (Fig. 2b), the per-panel normalization hiding intensity differences between AC and ZZ, and the differences in absorbed fluence (P11) and photoemission cross-section (P15) between AC and ZZ geometries, asking for unnormalized intensities on a common scale (P18); this is scored as 'partly'. For C6, P7 notes that holes depolarize and reverse under ZZ pumping (opposite to electrons), points out that optical readout of the electron-hole pair is therefore not nonvolatile in either channel, and asks what quantity serves as valley memory, but does not ask about other materials where electron and hole dynamics are not reversed; this is scored as 'partly'.
